title: Buddy Bolden and Seaforth's band; why Bolden gets the credit
summary: Laine says he played for money well before Bolden and would be older; Seaforth's band was military; he thinks New York people took the claims for granted.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. How long had you been playing for money before Buddy Bolden became well known? Oh, quite a while. Quite a while?
How many years? Ten years before Bolden?
I wouldn't... I couldn't say these things unless I was pretty much sure. Sure. You know? I know what you mean?

Well, you know, Papa, you're older than Bolden was, and they always talk about him being the first man. But you're older than him. Buddy Bolden? If he was alive, you'd be older than him. I'd be older than him? Oh, yeah. Yeah, of course I'd be older than Buddy Bolden.
Yeah. Sure. Sure. Sure. If he was alive, even so. He said I was still older than him. Yeah. Yeah.
Ask him about Seaforth's band. Yeah. Seaforth, yeah. How about the Seaforth band? Remember that?
He was a military band, too. Military. That's right. Yeah. He had a good orchestra. He had a good orchestra. They all straight stuff.

What about D.C.? I want to ask him about Bolden one more. Okay. I want to ask you one more about Bolden. How come Buddy Bolden gets all the credit for being the first when you were before Bolden playing ragtime? Okay. Why does he get the credit?
Well, those guys goes up to New York, you understand? I see. And, of course, up there and took what they said for granted.
